chemistry_takeaways: The latest measurements distinguish loading-associated displacement from interval widening: m211 shifts both endpoints at 50/1, whereas m82 completion barely changes with dose.

Alcohol, acid and carbonyl solvent responses depend on connectivity. m120's loading-associated decrease disappears at 1/1, while m119, m205, m200, m28 and m45 develop substantial retention over different ratio ranges.
Use density-derived masses consistently. The higher-loading m120 5/1 observation used 111.3 mg; the matched 1/1 and 2/1 higher-dose observations used 166.95 mg.
ml_takeaways: Recent m205, m28, m200 and m45 errors expose prospective response-transfer failures; adaptation around their acquired labels does not establish accuracy at another dose or ratio.
Interior ratio anchors and connected dose comparisons can distinguish curvature, endpoint displacement and completion broadening efficiently.
Duplicate physical inputs and crossed quantiles weaken numerical acquisition rankings. Additional loading labels are most useful where they discriminate a specific conditional response.
agreements: Learn onset and completion separately and preserve graph-specific condition responses.
Reduce further sampling of the locally resolved m82 and m27 questions.
Extend ordinary ester, ketone and aldehyde support alongside targeted follow-ups to recent failures.
disagreements: The advisers emphasize different m28 dose contrasts. I select a connected three-experiment design: lower- and higher-dose 10/1 measurements around the observed middle dose, plus a higher-dose 5/1 anchor.
For m76 and m16, I choose wider fixed-setup ratio contrasts than the ML memo's highlighted pairs.
Catalog inspection also favors m13, m128, m141, m195 and m206 continuations. Their sparse matched ratio support offers useful questions beyond the highlighted candidates.
expert_synthesis.planner_resolution: Select interpretable response measurements where outcomes can revise a concrete explanation, and add six unmeasured graphs with transferable chemical context. The batch emphasizes transition locations and conditional endpoint behavior. Further broad m82, m27, m73, m80, m124, m173 and m194 programs have lower immediate value.

batch_strategy: Select exactly 32 distinct eligible IDs across 20 molecules. Ten experiments introduce six graphs without observed labels: four fixed-setup ratio pairs and two haloarene anchors. Twenty-two experiments extend fourteen measured graphs. The batch contains eleven fixed-setup ratio pairs overall, with remaining additions connected to observed conditions. The m28 group combines a three-dose 10/1 comparison, including the observed middle dose, with a higher-dose ratio contrast. No selected full physical input duplicates another selection or an observed input. All stated masses are density-derived.

choices.reason: Measure m211 at 10/1 and 162.9 mg against its observed 54.3 mg counterpart. Determine whether the substantial loading-associated displacement measured at 50/1 already occurs at 10/1.
Measure m90 at 10/1 and 166.05 mg. Together with observed 110.7 mg 10/1 and both 5/1 doses, this tests whether its modest 5/1 dose response persists as completion becomes much later.
Add m119 at 2/1 and 105.8 mg between its matched measured 1/1 and 5/1 anchors, locating the rise in both endpoints without changing loading or injection conditions.

Measure m205 at 2/1 and 99 mg, directly extending its observed 99 mg 1/1 condition. This tests the predicted shallow initial response; the recent 49.5 mg 5/1 result remains a different-dose comparison.
Measure m200 in pure EA at 64.585 mg, preserving its observed 1/1 and 2/1 setup. Establish the strong-eluent boundary of its unexpectedly late nitroalcohol response.
Measure m28 at 10/1 and 58.4 mg against the observed 116.8 mg tail. Test whether late onset and completion persist after halving loading despite nearly invariant current dose predictions.
Measure m28 at 5/1 and 175.2 mg, providing an interior ratio anchor paired with the selected higher-dose 10/1 experiment under unchanged injection conditions.
Measure m28 at 10/1 and 175.2 mg. Complete the selected fixed-dose 5/1–10/1 pair and the loading comparison around the measured 116.8 mg 10/1 anchor.
Measure m45 at 5/1 and 85 mg, preserving both measured endpoint setups. Locate where delayed onset and later completion develop between 1/1 and 20/1.
Add m45 at 10/1 with the same 85 mg setup. With selected 5/1 and observed 1/1 and 20/1, constrain curvature rather than fitting a slope from two distant anchors.
Measure m164 at 5/1 and 104.77 mg between its matched measured 2/1 and 20/1 conditions, locating the response rise after its historical onset-decrease prediction failed.
Extend chalcone m165 to 20/1 at its observed 107.12 mg setup. Compare its within-molecule solvent response with m164 without assuming a common conjugated-ketone correction.
Introduce acetylfluorene m38 at 5/1 and 100 mg, establishing a baseline for a fixed-setup fused-aromatic ketone pair. Its 1000 uL DCM plug is retained within the pair.
Measure m38 at 20/1 with the same 100 mg setup. Test solvent-response transfer across fused carbonyl connectivity after heterogeneous measured ketone endpoint behavior.
Introduce biphenylaldehyde m189 at 2/1 and 110.7 mg, connecting observed biphenyl and aldehyde environments while establishing the stronger-eluent member of a matched pair.
Measure m189 at 20/1 with unchanged loading and DCM plug. Determine whether onset delay and completion response transfer to this ordinary aldehyde graph.
Introduce ethyl alpha-bromoisobutyrate m76 at 2/1 and 132.9 mg. Connect methyl/ethyl bromoester and alpha-substitution supervision under a fixed PE loading protocol.
Measure m76 at 20/1 with the same setup. Its predicted short interval remains untested; the ratio contrast supplies solvent dependence beyond a new molecular retention anchor.
Introduce branched-alkyl acrylate m16 at 5/1 and 44.25 mg, extending ordinary acrylate support beyond represented cyclic and long-chain ester graphs.
Measure m16 at 20/1 with unchanged loading and injection conditions. Test transfer of its predicted modest solvent response across alkyl branching and chain connectivity.
Introduce diiodobenzene m157 at 10/1 and 100 mg. Add a molecular anchor for iodine multiplicity in ordinary hydrophobic Row chemistry, recording its distinct 900 uL DCM plug.
Introduce the mixed Cl/Br/I arene m149 at 10/1 and 100 mg under DCM 300 uL loading. Extend heavy-halogen graph support at a common ratio without a further loading grid.
Measure multifunctional ester m13 at 2/1 and 168.3 mg, matching its measured 5/1 setup. Test the stronger-eluent response of its linked methacrylate and acetoacetate groups.
Extend m13 to 10/1 at the same 168.3 mg setup. The connected 2/1–5/1–10/1 curve tests transfer from simpler beta-ketoesters and ether-containing acetoacetates.
Measure naphthylmethanol m206 at 1/1 and 150 mg as the baseline of a matched pair. Test alcohol transfer from m205 while recognizing that side-chain length and ring attachment both differ.
Measure m206 at 5/1 with the same 150 mg setup, testing its predicted steep rise. Its existing 50 mg 2/1 observation provides context but is not a matched-dose intermediate.
Measure 2,6-dimethylpyridine m141 at 2/1 and 46 mg, directly extending its observed 46 mg 1/1 anchor and testing transfer to sterically flanked ring nitrogen.
Extend m141 to 10/1 at the same 46 mg setup. Learn its low-dose solvent response without treating the existing 138 mg 5/1 measurement as a matched intermediate.
Measure methylthioacetophenone m128 at 2/1 and 50 mg, preserving its measured 1/1 setup and anchoring a response pair beyond the available single-ratio observation.
Measure m128 at 20/1 with the same 50 mg setup. Test thioaryl-carbonyl solvent-response transfer in the context of the measured methylthioaldehyde curve.

Measure naphthaldehyde m195 at 2/1 and 150 mg, matching the setup of its nearly coincident, slightly reversed measured 20/1 endpoints. Add a stronger-eluent anchor without altering that recorded label.
Measure m195 at 10/1 and the same 150 mg setup. Constrain the separate onset and completion progression toward its measured 20/1 condition without imposing a shared naphthyl response.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen response is topology and condition dependent. Low-dose m211 retains broad 50/1 elution; its observed higher-dose 50/1 response mainly displaces both endpoints. m90 has a substantial fixed-dose rise through 10/1. The ratio range over which loading effects emerge remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected dose contrasts and a sterically distinct pyridine curve can teach conditional loading sensitivity without transferring a common nitrogen correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m211 loading displacement occur at 10/1, does m90 retain its modest loading effect there, and how does the fixed low-dose m141 curve develop?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol response transitions depend on connectivity and conditions. The m120 loading-associated decrease is absent at 1/1 but substantial at 2/1; m119, m205 and m200 develop late endpoints over different measured ratio ranges. A universal hydroxyl or dose correction is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Interior and strong-eluent anchors identify transition locations, while the m206 pair tests transfer to another naphthyl alcohol environment.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the m119 and m205 responses begin rising, how much does pure EA reduce m200 retention, and does m206 show a steep fixed-dose 1/1–5/1 response?

hypotheses.content: m28 has a measured steep 2/1–10/1 response at 116.8 mg, but persistence of its late 10/1 endpoints across loading and the position of its interior transition remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A connected dose series and ratio pair distinguish graph-level response learning from a loading-conditioned tail, where current predictions scarcely vary with dose.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do lower and higher 10/1 doses retain the measured late endpoints, and how much of the higher-dose response has developed by 5/1?

hypotheses.content: m45 and m46 have markedly different within-molecule solvent responses: the acid develops delayed onset and a wider interval, while the ester changes modestly. Different graph structures and loadings prevent assigning the entire contrast causally to esterification.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Interior acid measurements constrain nonlinear onset and completion responses beyond two distant ratio anchors and beyond the unusual cinnamic-acid curve.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m45 retention develop gradually through 5/1 and 10/1, or is most of the rise concentrated in one ratio range?

hypotheses.content: m164's measured weak-eluent onset delay and completion increase reject its historical predicted onset decrease. Transfer of this response to chalcone m165 remains unestablished.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An interior m164 anchor and a matched m165 extension separate solvent curvature from conjugated-carbonyl graph transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How much of m164's rise is present at 5/1, and does m165 develop a comparable response at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Represented acrylates, bromoesters and acetoacetate-containing esters exhibit substantially different retention and solvent sensitivity. Ester counts alone cannot supply their endpoint responses; transfer across alkyl substitution and additional carbonyl/ether connectivity needs direct supervision.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: New ordinary ester pairs and the connected m13 curve broaden graph support while preserving identifiable within-molecule solvent effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m16 and m76 retain modest responses across their selected ratios, and does multifunctional m13 follow the acquired beta-ketoester response through 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Ordinary non-hydroxyl graphs have heterogeneous onset and completion responses. The recorded m68 completion maximum, m201 weak-eluent overprediction, thioaryl-carbonyl retention and unusual m195 endpoint relation do not support a common aromatic or carbonyl correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: New fused-ketone and biphenyl-aldehyde pairs extend structural support; m128 and m195 continuations constrain sparsely anchored local curves without propagating another graph's behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do onset and completion slopes differ on the new ordinary graphs, and what progressions connect the existing m128 and m195 anchors to stronger eluent?

batch_rationale: The latest feedback favors locating conditional response transitions over repeating a general polarity correction. m211 and m90 receive direct dose contrasts at a discriminating ratio. m119, m205 and m200 receive economical additions connected to measured setups, while the m206 pair tests related alcohol transfer. The m28 group is one connected design: it tests whether the large acquired tail persists across doses and supplies a controlled interior solvent contrast. m45 and the conjugated ketones receive targeted curve measurements after large prospective slope errors. Six new graphs add ordinary ester, fused-carbonyl, aldehyde and heavy-halogen support. Catalog-derived m13, m128, m141 and m195 continuations address sparse curves in represented chemistry. These additions cover early, moderate and late elution and distinguish onset displacement from completion broadening.
expected_learning_value: Expected gains are better graph-conditioned solvent-transition locations, more reliable transfer across ordinary molecular environments, and improved conditional use of loading information. The m211 and m28 contrasts can distinguish changes in physical interval width from displacement of both endpoints. Null dose responses would also be informative after the m120 and m82 results. The matched pairs supervise both retention level and solvent dependence. Retraining improvement is expected qualitatively, not quantified; persistent condition-feature insensitivity and local record variation may limit gains.
feedback_interpretation:
Revise H_N_topology: observed 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4 measured low-dose m211 at 50/1 as 26.27/81.78 mL. Late completion therefore survives low loading. Relative to observed 434e465cfa7e0034f233 at same-dose 20/1, completion rises by 34.21 mL while recorded onset decreases by 2.61 mL. Against higher-dose 50/1 observation 0f06772820e6693753e3, both endpoints shift later by about 20–22 mL and interval widths remain similar. This supports a ratio-dependent completion response plus a loading-associated displacement, without establishing its mechanism. Observed 96710afeabc594baa359 measured m90 completion at 107.99 mL at 10/1, rejecting continued moderate retention inferred from earlier overpredictions.

Narrow H_OH_loading: observations 2bd6619109218dcf6580 and 880646809d9f015053f6 have nearly equal m120 1/1 endpoints across 55.65 and 166.95 mg. The large earlier-elution shift at 2/1 does not persist at 1/1. Correct the earlier dose interpretation: e4fd83fb3852eb354a66 used 111.3 mg at 5/1, so only the 1/1 and 2/1 records complete the identical two-dose comparison. The fixed-dose rises in 776ee2c1e85ebde75168, 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2 and a92f7617b135de150588 strengthen graph-specific alcohol response learning, but do not establish a shared dose law.

Locally resolve the m82 loading question: 61090cfdcf019e0891a3 and b6bf451b4911ee22d4a4 have completions of 64.40 and 64.37 mL, while onset moves earlier by 2.10 mL. This resembles m94's descriptive completion stability and reduces the value of another extensive loading grid, without establishing statistical equivalence. New m27 follow-ups 59d8c3d932aece6945ae and f5e5ad6e9b48aa9731b5 were accurately predicted, also reducing immediate continuation value.

Strengthen the ordinary-response question selectively: new m68 points preserve its recorded completion maximum near 5/1, but do not establish same-input reproducibility. m28 observation 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a and m45 observation b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1 reveal large solvent-response underprediction; m46 remains much less responsive. Observation b7fffd840d208b29776c rejects m164's predicted onset decrease. Conversely, m201 weak-eluent predictions were too late. These directions require conditional learning. m3 contains no carbonyl and remains separate evidence. Preserve both conflicting m73 records and the slightly reversed m195 measurement without silently correcting either. Earlier m194 results establish recurrence across conditions, not same-input reproducibility.

Only observed records establish measurements. Candidate predictions remain prospective, V2 minus V1 is physical elution interval width, and quantile widths are not treated as calibrated uncertainty. Adaptive historical errors identify useful questions but do not estimate unbiased overall Row error or demonstrate retraining improvement.
